items.title: Eritrea accuses Ethiopia of seeking regime change
items.quote: openly working to bring about regime change in Eritrea
points: Said Ethiopia is shielding and supporting what he called mercenaries posing as opposition.
Earlier called Ethiopia's accusations of Eritrean involvement "false flags" to justify war, as reported by Euronews.
Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing Tigray rebels. Neither government answered questions about the fighting.

items.role: EU statement, as reported by The Media Line
items.title: EU calls for halt to violence and warns Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions could spread
points: Called for an immediate halt to escalating violence in Ethiopia and warned the conflict could spread across the Horn of Africa.
Asked outside powers not to interfere and to respect the sovereignty of states.
Urged the parties to implement the Pretoria cessation of hostilities agreement through the African Union, protect civilians and allow humanitarian access.

items.role: Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General, daily briefing
items.title: UN says aid warehouse looted in Tigray and civilian casualties are growing
items.quote: Humanitarian personnel, premises and assets must never be targeted and must be protected at all times.
points: Expressed deep concern about growing reports of civilian casualties, including among displaced people, in northern Ethiopia.
Said a UN agency warehouse and facilities of local and international aid groups were looted in Tigray, with food, seed, fertilizer and water pumps lost.
Said phone and electronic banking services resumed in most of Tigray after more than a week, and aid deliveries to Tigray and Afar are planned to resume.

items.role: Ethiopian Prime Minister, speaking in Parliament at his swearing-in
items.title: Abiy says Ethiopia will keep seeking access to the Red Sea
items.quote: Based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea
points: Said Ethiopia will work to secure an outlet to the sea.
Spoke at his swearing-in for another five-year term, as fighting continues in Tigray.
Four Red Sea states said earlier that only coastal states should govern the waterway.

items.issuer: Leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan
items.role: Joint declaration after a meeting in New Alamein, Egypt
items.title: Four leaders issue joint declaration as Ethiopia war escalates
items.quote: a dialogue, not confrontation
points: Called for dialogue on cross-border challenges in the region.
Said the Red Sea should remain under the authority of coastal states.
Egypt and Sudan warned against what they called unilateral measures harming downstream countries on the Nile.

items.title: Egypt's president urges dialogue as violence continues in Ethiopia
items.quote: dialogue, not confrontation
points: Said cross-border challenges require cooperation, not competition.
Called for dialogue and consultation, away from unilateral policies or narrow interests.
Spoke at a meeting in El-Alamein, Egypt, with leaders of Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan, as reported by the Taipei Times.

items.title: TPLF says it has left Mekelle and the regional government will operate elsewhere
items.quote: temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else
points: Said it had retreated from Mekelle, the Tigray capital.
Said the regional government would operate from another location.
Ethiopian government and allied forces have said they control the city; this is as reported by TRT World.

items.title: TPLF chairman says the fighting continues the previous war
points: Said the current fighting is a "continuation of the previous war", as reported by AP.
Said TPLF forces would keep attacking and defending the region.
AP reported the TPLF left Mekelle to spare the city from destruction.

items.title: US urges Ethiopia and Eritrea to show restraint
items.quote: The Horn of Africa cannot sustain another military conflict and humanitarian crisis.
points: Said rising cross-border tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea could affect the whole region.
Urged both countries to respect their neighbours' sovereignty and territorial integrity and to exercise maximum restraint.
Called for a return to dialogue, as agreed in their 2018 peace framework.

items.role: Tigere Chagutah, Regional Director for East and Southern Africa
items.title: African Union must convene an emergency session on Ethiopia as the conflict expands
items.quote: The AU, which was one of the guarantors of the ceasefire agreement that has now effectively collapsed, must learn from past mistakes
points: Called on the African Union Peace and Security Council to hold an emergency session on the renewed war in Tigray, Afar and Amhara.
Raised alarm over reports of intensified aerial attacks across Tigray and damage to civilian infrastructure, including schools.
Warned that communication blackouts have often hidden atrocities and cut civilians off from the outside world.

items.title: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia
points: Said Ethiopia's expulsion of its diplomats left it no choice but to respond in kind.
Announced it was cutting diplomatic relations with Ethiopia.
Has repeatedly denied supporting the armed alliance fighting Ethiopia's government.

items.title: Ethiopia closes its embassy in Asmara and expels 10 Eritrean diplomats
items.quote: direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence against Ethiopia
points: Accused Eritrea of hostile acts against Ethiopia.
Ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours and announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara.
Eritrea has denied involvement.

items.title: AU Commission urges Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt to avoid escalation
items.quote: exercise maximum restraint and refrain from actions or statements that could further escalate tensions
points: Called on Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt to show maximum restraint.
Urged the three countries to settle differences through diplomatic channels and dialogue.
Said it stands ready to support de-escalation and peaceful resolution of differences.

items.role: Sheikh Shakhboot bin Nahyan Al Nahyan, Minister of State
items.title: UAE declares solidarity with Ethiopia's government
items.quote: full solidarity with the government and people
points: Said the UAE stands with the government and people of Ethiopia.
Rejected attempts to change Ethiopia's constitutional order by force.

items.title: Qatar calls for an end to the fighting and respect for the Pretoria Agreement
items.quote: an immediate end to the fighting, protection for civilians and respect for the Pretoria Peace Agreement
points: Condemned what it described as military escalation against Ethiopian federal forces.
Called for civilians to be protected.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV appeals for dialogue in Tigray, Afar and Amhara
items.quote: Armed conflict never solves problems but only worsens them leaving in its wake a trail of death, destruction and resentment
points: Appealed for peace in Tigray and the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions.
Invited all parties to choose the path of dialogue.
Hoped the international community would give generous and timely humanitarian aid.

items.role: Abdullahi Boru Halakhe, Senior Advocate for East and Southern Africa
items.title: Tigray: immediate action needed to reverse the course of war
items.quote: Ethiopia is sliding into a regional war.
points: Warned that drone strikes have damaged humanitarian aid convoys.
Reported that more than 95% of displaced households face moderate to severe food insecurity.
Called for an immediate ceasefire and a return to negotiations under the Pretoria Agreement.

items.title: Hospitals see a surge in war-wounded patients as fighting resumes
points: War-wounded patients at Korem and Alamata hospitals rose from about 180 to more than 420 within 48 hours (22–25 September).
More than 300 war-wounded patients reached Suhul Hospital in Shire by 25 September.
Suspended work at Alamata Hospital and moved staff to hospitals seeing the sharpest rise in wounded.

items.title: EU provides €61 million in humanitarian aid amid rapidly deteriorating situation in Ethiopia
points: €61 million for people affected by conflict, displacement, disease and climate hazards across Ethiopia.
Funds food, nutrition, health care, clean water, shelter, protection and education in emergencies.
Calls for immediate de-escalation, protection of civilians and unimpeded humanitarian access.

items.role: Field Marshal Birhanu Jula, Chief of General Staff
items.title: Army chief accuses Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt of backing the rebel alliance
points: Accused Eritrea of mobilising financial support for the TPLF.
Accused Sudan and Egypt of backing the armed groups fighting federal troops.
Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt have all rejected the accusations.

items.issuer: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
items.title: UN rights chief alarmed by civilian toll as fighting intensifies in Ethiopia
points: Said he was alarmed by the mounting toll on civilians and called on all parties to protect civilians and urgently de-escalate.

Cited reported airstrikes by Ethiopian forces on five schools in Tigray on 22 September and a mortar strike in Kobo, Amhara, on 23 September. These reports are as relayed by JURIST and are unverified here.
Raised concern about reported forced recruitment of civilians and children by the TPLF and arbitrary conscription by government forces.

items.title: Indiscriminate airstrike on a residential compound in Mekelle
items.quote: The resumption of hostilities in northern Ethiopia heightens concerns about unlawful attacks and the grave threat posed to civilians.
points: Found that an apparent Ethiopian government airstrike on 20 August hit a residential compound for teachers and their families in Mekelle's Daero neighbourhood.
Thirteen civilians were wounded, including seven children. Residents saw no military presence at the compound.
Said the attack may be a war crime and called for those responsible to be investigated and prosecuted.

items.role: Taye Atske Selassie, at the UN General Assembly
items.title: Ethiopia's president warns of foreign interference at the UN
items.quote: We urge them to respect the sacred right of the people of the Horn of Africa to live in peace and prosperity.
points: Blamed “external actors” for the renewed conflict, in remarks widely read as aimed at Egypt and Eritrea.
Spoke as fighting spread from Tigray into Afar and Amhara.

items.role: UN Spokesperson and UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
items.title: UN voices grave concern as fighting spreads across northern Ethiopia
items.quote: exercise maximum restraint
points: Raised concern over the use of drones and harm to civilians.
Volker Türk reported airstrikes hit five schools in Tigray on Sept 22, and a mortar strike killed civilians in Kobo, Amhara, on Sept 24.
A drone strike destroyed a truck carrying food aid in northwestern Tigray; road closures are disrupting aid.

items.title: UK statement on escalation in northern Ethiopia
items.quote: Civilians must be protected, and those affected by the conflict must be able to access basic services and life-saving aid.
points: Condemned attacks by the Tigray Defence Forces in Afar and southern Tigray, and the takeover of Tigray's airports.
Called on all parties to halt hostilities and support African Union mediation.
Called for safe, unhindered humanitarian access and protection of aid workers.

items.title: Army says its counter-offensive inflicted heavy losses in North Wollo
points: Said government forces launched a counter-offensive after the TPLF and its allies attacked areas of North Wollo, Amhara.
Said 272 Tigrayan fighters were killed. This figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: Renewed Tigray fighting shows the need to protect civilians
items.quote: The parties need to take all necessary measures to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.
points: Warned that the renewed fighting raises serious concerns for civilians, given past atrocities and the lack of accountability for them.
Urged international actors to act immediately to protect civilians and support strong monitoring.

items.role: Ambassador Ervin J. Massinga, U.S. Embassy Addis Ababa
items.title: Statement on recent developments in Tigray and Afar
items.quote: I still believe a reasonable political dialogue is the right way to go.
points: Disappointed by the TPLF leadership's decision to launch a large-scale offensive.
Criticised the rejection of AU-sponsored dialogue led by President Obasanjo.
Said the U.S. has tools to impose further sanctions on those undermining Ethiopia's stability.

items.role: Getachew Reda, adviser to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed
items.title: Government says the TPLF launched an “all-out offensive”
points: Said the TPLF seized federally controlled airports in Tigray.
Said the TPLF launched an all-out offensive against government positions in Afar and Amhara.

items.title: Statement by the Spokesperson on the situation in Northern Ethiopia
items.quote: Immediate de-escalation is needed. It is not yet too late to decisively recommit to the Permanent Cessation of Hostilities Agreement.
points: Deeply concerned by the takeover of the Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports by TPLF forces.
Concerned by several drone strikes carried out by the Ethiopian National Defence Force in recent weeks.
Strongly condemned strikes affecting humanitarian convoys and any denial of humanitarian access.

items.title: IGAD calls for immediate de-escalation in northern Ethiopia
items.quote: cease hostilities, exercise maximum restraint and refrain from any action that could further imperil civilian lives
points: Concerned by renewed hostilities, the seizure of civilian airports and disrupted air travel.
Called the Pretoria Agreement the only legitimate framework for resolving disputes.
Urged direct dialogue and warned neighbouring countries against making tensions worse.

items.title: AUC Chairperson calls for utmost restraint and immediate de-escalation in northern Ethiopia
items.quote: the cornerstone of sustainable peace, stability and reconciliation in Ethiopia
points: Deeply concerned by the seizure of the Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports and the detention of federal personnel by the TPLF.
Said the 2022 Pretoria Agreement remains the foundation for peace (quoted above).
Asked AU High Representative Olusegun Obasanjo to re-engage the parties.

items.title: Secretary-General urges restraint as fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia
items.quote: exercise maximum restraint, immediately de-escalate tensions, protect civilians
points: Gravely concerned by the seizure of the Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports and the spread of fighting.
Called for safe and unhindered humanitarian access.
Backed African Union mediation led by former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, under the Pretoria Agreement.

items.title: Tigray authorities say they have entered a “defensive war”
points: Said the federal government launched an open invasion of Tigray with aircraft, drones and infantry on Sept 22–23.
Said Tigray's forces had been instructed to defend against the attack.
Called for unity among Tigray's army, people and allied forces.

items.role: State Department, Bureau of African Affairs
items.title: U.S. condemns drone strike on Catholic Relief Services convoy in Tigray
points: Condemned the Sept 20 drone strike on a truck carrying about 41 tonnes of food for displaced families in Sheraro.
Urged authorities to conduct a full investigation and share the findings.
Called on the parties to engage in dialogue.

items.title: Federal government suspends Tigrai TV indefinitely
points: Suspended the regional broadcaster Tigrai TV indefinitely.
Barred other media outlets from broadcasting its reports.
Six days later, on Sept 27, a drone strike hit Tigrai TV's headquarters in Mekelle.

items.role: Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival
items.title: Seven armed groups announce an alliance to remove Prime Minister Abiy
points: The TPLF, the Oromo Liberation Army, the Amhara Fano National Movement, the ONLF and three other groups announced a joint alliance.
Said their aim is to remove Abiy Ahmed's government and replace it with an inclusive transitional government.
The announcement was read on Tigrai TV. Full-scale fighting began two days later.

items.title: Rising Tigray tensions test the African Union
items.quote: Both parties have accused the other of military mobilization, while unresolved questions over contested territories, the safe return of displaced people, and disarmament threaten the agreement.
points: Warned that disputes over the Pretoria Agreement were pushing the parties toward war.
Reported that the TPLF had forcibly recruited civilians in Tigray, including children as young as 15.
Documented continuing abuses against Tigrayans by authorities and security forces in Western Tigray.

items.issuer: 41 countries at the UN Human Rights Council
items.role: Delivered by Lithuania's Ambassador Rytis Paulauskas
items.title: Joint statement on the human rights situation in Ethiopia
items.quote: Another devastating conflict should be avoided at any cost and differences between parties should be resolved via political dialogue.
points: Warned that a new military confrontation in Tigray would have severe consequences for a region already facing drought.
Called for immediate de-escalation and adherence to the 2022 Pretoria Agreement.
Fully supported the AU-led mediation process.

items.role: Ambassador Ervin Massinga and Walter Parks, U.S. Mission to the AU
items.title: U.S. urges continued engagement with AU envoy Obasanjo
items.quote: We look forward to engaging former President Obasanjo
points: Said Obasanjo's role under his African Union mandate remains critical, and hoped he would return to Tigray soon.
Warned of growing fears that the conflict could resume.
Urged priority for the drought response and the safe return of displaced people.

items.issuer: EU, Canada, Norway, UK and US
items.role: Joint statement by diplomatic missions in Addis Ababa
items.title: International partners warn that renewed war would be devastating
items.quote: We are following developments in northern Ethiopia with deep concern.
points: Signed by the EU, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, Canada, Norway, the UK and the US, among others.
Urged all parties to implement the Pretoria Agreement constructively and in good faith.
Backed African Union mediation led by Olusegun Obasanjo, and warned a new war would be devastating for a drought-hit region.

items.issuer: Office of the Tigray Regional President
items.title: Tigray says talks with AU envoy Obasanjo brought no progress
items.quote: neither the appetite nor the political space
points: Said Obasanjo's Aug 24 visit to Mekelle brought no new proposals from the federal government.
Listed five unresolved issues: the economic embargo, military encirclement, occupied territories, return of displaced people, and the TPLF's legal status.
Said it would not repeat a process of talks and unfulfilled promises (quoted above).

items.title: TPLF says drones struck residential areas of Mekelle
points: Said one strike hit a residential area of Mekelle and a second hit near Mekelle University.
Ayder Hospital reported at least 13 people injured, including 5 children and 7 women.
Ethiopia's federal army did not immediately comment.

items.title: Tigray accuses the federal government of a drone strike near Mekelle
points: Said a drone hit a farmer training centre in Dandera village, about 15 km from Mekelle.
Said there were no injuries; a local witness reported one fighter killed and two wounded.
Ethiopia's federal army did not comment.

items.role: Tigere Chagutah, Regional Director for East and Southern Africa
items.title: Tigray residents at renewed risk of human rights violations as violence returns
items.quote: The resumption of violence in Tigray region puts residents at renewed risk of human rights violations
points: Warned after clashes on 1 August between Tigrayan forces and the Ethiopian army.
Called on federal and Tigrayan authorities to respect human rights, and raised concerns about media restrictions and forced conscription by Tigrayan authorities.
Urged the restoration of international human rights investigations in Ethiopia.

items.title: Federal government blames the TPLF for clashes in Western Tigray
items.quote: Enough war! Let us resolve our differences through dialogue.
points: Accused TPLF forces of starting the fighting near the Sudanese border.
PM adviser Getachew Reda urged Tigray Defence Forces commanders to break with TPLF chairman Debretsion Gebremichael.

items.title: Tigray says federal forces attacked at dawn in Western Tigray
points: Said federal forces opened an assault at dawn, advancing from Shererina near the Sudanese border.
Described the fighting as a threat to Tigray's “national survival” and called on Tigrayans to prepare.

items.title: EU urges de-escalation and respect for the 2022 peace agreement
items.quote: It is imperative that another devastating conflict is avoided, and that differences between parties are resolved via political dialogue.
points: Expressed serious concern about developments in Tigray.
Urged immediate de-escalation and adherence to the November 2022 Pretoria Agreement.

items.title: Persecution of Tigrayans in Western Tigray is unrelenting
items.quote: Tigrayans in Western Tigray Zone are facing severe and dehumanizing restrictions on all aspects of their lives.
points: Found that Tigrayans in Western Tigray face arbitrary arrest, are refused ID cards and need hard-to-get permits to travel.
Reported that more than 740,000 people displaced from Western Tigray remain in camps in central Tigray.
Called for officials implicated in abuses to be suspended and investigated, and for targeted sanctions.

items.issuer: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
items.title: UN rights chief fears a new crisis in Tigray
items.quote: Both sides must step back from the brink and work to resolve their differences through political means
points: Warned of renewed heavy fighting from 26 January, with drones, artillery and heavy weapons.
Raised concern about civilians being arrested because of their perceived affiliations.
Noted that about one million people remain displaced from the 2020–2022 war.

items.role: Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member
items.title: Statement on the resumption of hostilities in northern Tigray
items.quote: The recent fighting in Tigray risks embroiling Ethiopia back into a civil war that endangers millions of lives
points: Called for an immediate ceasefire and full humanitarian access.
Urged full implementation of the 2022 Cessation of Hostilities Agreement.

items.title: MSF concludes Ethiopian soldiers deliberately killed its three staff in 2021
items.quote: They were fully identifiable as humanitarian workers and were shot several times at close range while facing their attackers.
points: Concluded that María Hernández, Yohannes Halefom Reda and Tedros Gebremariam Gebremichael were deliberately killed by members of Ethiopia's military in June 2021.
Said they were not killed by accident or in crossfire.

items.title: Report finds strong evidence of acts of genocide against Tigrayans
points: Concluded there is strong evidence that Ethiopian forces and their allies committed acts of genocide against Tigrayans as an ethnic group.
Listed killings, serious bodily and mental harm, measures to prevent births, and conditions of life calculated to destroy the group.
Called for Ethiopia to be brought before the International Court of Justice.

items.title: Sexual violence in Tigray was widespread and systematic, and continued after the truce
items.quote: these incidents of conflict-related sexual violence were both widespread and systematic
points: Reviewed 305 medical records from Tigray's health facilities; 304 documented conflict-related sexual violence.
Most attacks involved several perpetrators, identified as Eritrean or Ethiopian armed forces.
128 of the incidents happened after the November 2022 peace agreement.

items.title: Ethnic cleansing persists under the Tigray truce
items.quote: The November truce in northern Ethiopia has not brought about an end to the ethnic cleansing of Tigrayans in Western Tigray Zone.
points: Found that Amhara forces and local authorities kept forcibly expelling Tigrayans after the truce.
More than 1,000 Tigrayans were held in detention sites in Humera, Rawyan and Adebai, where some died of starvation and lack of medicine.

items.title: UN chief welcomes the Pretoria peace agreement
items.quote: a critical first step towards ending the devastating two-year old conflict
points: Welcomed the signing of the Permanent Cessation of Hostilities Agreement in Pretoria.
Urged the international community to support the agreement and the parties to keep negotiating in a spirit of reconciliation.

items.role: Joint report: “We Will Erase You from This Land”
items.title: Crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray
points: Concluded that Amhara officials and forces, with the acquiescence and possible participation of federal forces, carried out a campaign of ethnic cleansing against Tigrayans.
Documented killings, sexual violence, mass detention, denial of aid and the forced removal of hundreds of thousands of people.
Based on more than 400 interviews; called for accountability and an African Union-led peacekeeping force.

items.title: WHO chief says the blockade has created “hell” in Tigray
items.quote: Nowhere in the world are we witnessing hell like in Tigray
points: Said the blockade was stopping food and medicine from reaching Tigray and called it an insult to humanity.
Said all WHO requests for permission to deliver life-saving medicines had been refused.

items.role: Special session on Ethiopia, requested by the European Union
items.title: UN sets up an international commission to investigate abuses in Ethiopia
points: Voted 21 to 15, with 11 abstentions, to create the International Commission of Human Rights Experts on Ethiopia.
Gave it a mandate to investigate violations committed since 3 November 2020.

items.title: UN aid chief calls Tigray's hunger crisis “a stain on our conscience”
items.quote: This is man-made, this can be remedied by the act of government.
points: Described a de facto blockade of food, medicine and fuel to Tigray.
Said Tigray needed 100 aid trucks a day, but only about 10% had got through in the previous three months.

items.role: Report: “I Don't Know If They Realized I Was a Person”
items.title: Troops and militia raped and abducted women and girls in Tigray
points: Based on interviews with 63 survivors, found that women and girls were raped, held in sexual slavery and tortured by Ethiopian and Eritrean soldiers, Amhara special forces and Fano militia.
Concluded the violations amount to war crimes and may amount to crimes against humanity.

items.title: Three MSF staff killed in an attack in Tigray
items.quote: No words can truly convey all our sadness, shock and outrage against this horrific attack.
points: María Hernández, Yohannes Halefom Reda and Tedros Gebremariam Gebremichael were found dead beside their vehicle on 24 June 2021.

items.title: UN declares famine in Tigray
items.quote: There is famine now in Tigray.
points: More than 350,000 people in Tigray were found to be living in famine conditions.
Said it was the highest number of people in famine anywhere in the world since 2011 in Somalia.

items.role: Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the UK, the US and the EU High Representative
items.title: G7 statement on the situation in Tigray
items.quote: All parties must exercise utmost restraint, ensure the protection of civilians and respect human rights and international law.
points: Condemned killings, sexual violence, indiscriminate shelling and forced displacement.
Called for an independent investigation and immediate, unhindered humanitarian access.
Welcomed the announced withdrawal of Eritrean forces from Tigray.

items.role: Secretary of State Antony Blinken, testifying to Congress
items.title: U.S. Secretary of State describes “acts of ethnic cleansing” in Western Tigray
items.quote: acts of ethnic cleansing, which we've seen in Western Tigray
points: Called for Eritrean and Amhara forces to leave Tigray.
Called for unhindered humanitarian access and an independent investigation of abuses.

items.issuer: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
items.title: UN rights chief says war crimes may have been committed by multiple parties in Tigray
points: Said serious violations, possibly amounting to war crimes and crimes against humanity, may have been committed by the Ethiopian army, the TPLF, Eritrean forces, and Amhara regional forces and militia.
Cited corroborated reports of mass killings in Axum and Dengelat by Eritrean forces, and indiscriminate shelling in Mekelle, Humera and Adigrat.
Called for an objective, independent investigation.

items.title: Atrocities in Ethiopia's Tigray region
items.quote: the immediate withdrawal of Eritrean forces and Amhara regional forces from Tigray
points: Said the U.S. was gravely concerned by reported atrocities in Tigray.
Condemned killings, forced removals, sexual assaults and other serious abuses.
Called for an end to hostilities and unhindered delivery of aid.

items.role: Deprose Muchena, Director for East and Southern Africa
items.title: Eritrean troops' massacre of hundreds of civilians in Axum may be a crime against humanity
items.quote: Ethiopian and Eritrean troops carried out multiple war crimes in their offensive to take control of Axum.
points: Found that Eritrean troops systematically killed hundreds of unarmed civilians in Axum on 28–29 November 2020.
Based on 41 survivors and witnesses; satellite images showed signs of mass burials near two churches.
Called for a UN-led investigation and full access to Tigray.

items.title: UN chief alarmed by clashes in Tigray, calls for immediate de-escalation
items.quote: deeply alarmed over the situation in the Tigray region of Ethiopia
points: Issued on the day the war began.
Called for immediate steps to de-escalate tensions and a peaceful resolution.
